To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1,N6 ethenoadenine (epsilon A), a mutagenic lesion formed by vinyl chloride, exhibits ambiguous base pairing potential and is capable of substituting for all four normal bases (A, G, C, and T) during DNA replication, catalyzed in vitro by E. coli DNA polymerase.
the major form of epsilon dAMP misincorporation during DNA synthesis is replacement of A and that this occurs by an ambiguous base pairing mechanism.

epsilon dATPs can substitute for all four normal dNTPS during DNA synthesis, and the degree of incorporation of each epsilon dATP opposite the template bases varies considerably along the template, with the most efficient incorporation occurring at positions where the template base is A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidation of the molecular mechanisms by which vinyl chloride (VC)-induced mutagenicity is manifested.
the mechanism by which 1,N6-Etheno-adenine (Ea) is formed in DNA.
the base pairing properties of the major adduct of the carcinogen vinyl chloride in mammalian cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

epsilon dATPs, like the other etheno dNTPs (epsilon dGTP and epsilon dCTP), are capable of incorporation opposite all template nucleotides, but that the extent of incorporation is dependent upon the template nucleotide, the template sequence, and the site of incorporation within a template.
epsilon A is not an efficient substrate for DNA polymerase I.
epsilon dATPs are misincorporated into DNA by DNA polymerase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
epsilon dATPs are not likely to be mutagenic in vivo.

epsilon A is a poor substrate for DNA polymerase I, that the enzyme does not exhibit a strong preference for epsilon A opposite template T, and that epsilon A can substitute for G and C in addition to A.

the etheno modification of dAMP does not appear to be a good model for the mutagenic lesion induced by vinyl chloride in mammalian cells, although the etheno modification is clearly capable of producing a variety of base pair substitutions in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the etheno modification of A is not a strong mutagenic lesion, but it does exhibit some base pairing ambiguity that may contribute to mutagenesis.
, although epsilon dATP exhibits ambiguous base pairing, it is not a good template for DNA polymerase I.
epsilon A is a poor substrate for E. coli DNA polymerase, and that its incorporation during DNA synthesis is not as simple as replacement of A.
